tech.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman confirmed on the Sources podcast that the company will build its own humanoid robot — 'We will' — with a 'cool demo' expected in 2027, though robots on streets will take a few more years. Altman said the human form makes sense because the world is designed for people, and stressed the AI 'brain' matters more than the body. OpenAI is hiring across motion control, actuators and manufacturing.
tech.title: Altman confirms OpenAI will build a humanoid robot, demo in 2027

tech.summary: Anthropic has been pitching US lawmakers on its own draft AI safety bill, per a Politico report. The proposal would let the government block a model's release only for foreseeable, imminent risks above $1bn in damages or 50+ deaths or severe injuries, tied to bioweapons, model evasion or cyberattacks — plus independent evaluations registered with the Commerce Department that must report 'imminent enumerated risk' within 72 hours.
tech.title: Anthropic takes its AI safety bill to Capitol Hill

tech.summary: The IMF's October 2026 Global Financial Stability Report examined 14 disclosed AI transactions since 2023: about $300bn in equity, $650bn in debt and $1.4 trillion in future revenue commitments — with 'circular financing' where investors fund AI firms that then commit to buy back their products. The fund warns weaker-than-expected AI profitability could trigger asset corrections, magnified by leverage and concentration.
tech.title: IMF flags $650bn AI financing loop as financial-stability risk

tech.summary: Asian equities fell on Monday as Friday's Wall Street tech rout carried into the week: Japan's Nikkei dropped 2.15%, the Kospi shed 1.6%, and GIFT Nifty pointed red. Traders braced for China's Q3 GDP data, 70+ S&P 500 earnings this week (including Tesla and Meta), the Fed's pre-meeting blackout, and persistent doubts over whether massive AI spending will pay off. Brent stayed near $108 a barrel.
tech.title: Asian stocks slide as tech rout, China GDP and big earnings weigh

tech.summary: IBM has deployed about 6,000 AI agents across 150+ consulting workflows through its IBM Consulting Advantage platform, and now sells the same 'human-digital team' playbook to clients. Senior VP Mohamad Ali says a security-threat investigation that took 45 minutes now takes agents two minutes plus ten of human review — though he admits some agent deployments show 'negative productivity' and get rolled back.
tech.title: IBM deploys 6,000 AI agents across consulting workflows

pakistan.summary: PPP chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari said the federal government could lift emergency and governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa if the opposition engages with Islamabad on a united anti-terrorism plan. Speaking in Karachi on the Karsaz bombing anniversary, he defended the federal takeover, criticised the KP chief minister for not facing terrorists, and warned Pakistan faces a 'historic economic crisis' that also demands fighting terrorism.
pakistan.title: Bilawal says KP emergency can end if opposition engages Centre on counterterrorism

pakistan.summary: Salman Ali Agha's 107 off 90 balls and captain Shaheen Shah Afridi's 3-55 powered Pakistan to a 37-run win over Sri Lanka in the ODI Tri-Nation Series opener at Rawalpindi. Pakistan posted 305 in 49.5 overs; Sri Lanka were bowled out for 268 despite a 119-run fifth-wicket stand between Pavan Rathnayake (79) and Janith Liyanage (60). Pakistan next face England on Tuesday.
pakistan.title: Salman Agha's ton, Shaheen's 3-55 seal 37-run win over Sri Lanka in tri-series opener

pakistan.summary: Federal government debt rose by an average of Rs20 billion per day, adding Rs18.143 trillion over the past two-and-a-half years to reach Rs82.953 trillion by August 2026, according to State Bank of Pakistan documents. Domestic debt climbed Rs16.082 trillion; total public debt grew 7.7% year-on-year to Rs86.715 trillion.
pakistan.title: Govt debt swells by Rs18.14 trillion in two-and-a-half years

pakistan.summary: Foreign investment in Pakistan's domestic bonds reached $188 million in the first nine days of October — $78m in T-bills and $110m in Pakistan Investment Bonds — with Gulf investors, led by the UAE ($130m), showing strong interest. Since the fiscal year began, total foreign investment in government securities has hit $656m, against $41.5bn in record remittances in FY26.
pakistan.title: Gulf investors pour $188m into Pakistan domestic bonds in early October

pakistan.summary: LPG stakeholders urged the government to move from monthly to daily pricing and delink rates from Saudi Aramco's Contract Price, after prices rose Rs100 per kg over the weekend. The Rahimdad-250 border closure disrupted supplies — 70% of Pakistan's 2m tonnes annual LPG use is imported — and 4,500 tonnes are reportedly stranded on the Iranian side, with winter demand rising.
pakistan.title: LPG stakeholders demand daily pricing amid soaring rates

pakistan.summary: The Federal Board of Revenue will brief Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif today on the rollout of the faceless system on the Inland Revenue side, use of AI for returns analysis, and a transformation plan to close a tax gap of over Rs1 trillion across 18 sectors. Digital monitoring is fully installed in sugar, cement, tobacco, tiles and fertilisers, with more sectors to follow by October 30.
pakistan.title: FBR to brief PM today on faceless system, AI-based tax reforms
